newsitem.title: FRANCE: FRENCH BOND FUTURES END LITTLE CHANGED.
newsitem.headline: FRENCH BOND FUTURES END LITTLE CHANGED.

text.p: French bond futures closed little changed after a weaker open in the United States prevented the September contract from breaking through a stiff area of resistance below 129.50.

The contract opened lower following a decline in U.S. bonds on Friday but moved into positive territory, boosted by a bout of short covering and helped by the relative health of the mark a day ahead the Bundesbank's next money market tender.
Fears that a slide in the mark towards 1.90 per dollar could prompt a shift to higher short-term German interest rates as soon as Tuesday had plagued debt markets last week.

Traders said the decline below 129 early in the day gave some a chance to close out short positions taken last week but slim volumes, concern ahead of U.S. retail sales figures Wednesday and the German tender kept prices capped.
The yield spread between French and German 10-year bonds was unchanged at minus seven basis points.

Waning fears of an interest rate rise in Germany also helped PIBOR contracts stage a small recovery after suffering heavy losses in recent days. September rose two basis points with short covering again the main driving force, traders said.
The French franc moved higher against the mark to a high of 3.3677.
